section_summary: This section begins with a Japanese Economic Stabilization Board plan for the 1949 economy, including a single exchange rate, price and wage measures, fiscal restraint, food supply, production targets, and trade programs. Subsequent correspondence and reports discuss the Dodge program, Japanese industry and trade, deconcentration, coal production, and reactions to stabilization. The section ends partway through a paper proposing public education and economic incentives to build support for the program.

subfiles.title: Outline of Over-all Measures
subfiles.doc_type: enclosure; Economic Stabilization Board policy plan and statistical tables
subfiles.about: Proposes measures to stabilize Japan's economy and finance its rehabilitation in 1949.
subfiles.summary: The plan calls for a single exchange rate, limited trade and price subsidies, adjustments to basic material prices, standard wages, and balanced public finance. It sets priorities for food supply, industrial investment, production, and exports. Tables provide national accounts, funding estimates, production and food targets, trade programs, and industry funding requirements.

subfiles.title: Suggested Visit of Mr. Joseph Dodge to the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Suggests that Dodge brief the Far Eastern Commission during his visit to Washington.
subfiles.summary: Commission delegations want Dodge to discuss Japan's stabilization program and recovery outlook.

subfiles.title: “News Article” on American Economic Policy in Japan
subfiles.from: LaRue R. Lutkins, American Vice Consul, Kunming
subfiles.about: Forwards a translated Cheng Yi Pao article and notes the paper's recent anti-American turn.
subfiles.summary: Lutkins encloses the article and describes the newspaper's changed editorial stance.

subfiles.title: Article on American support for Japanese armaments industry
subfiles.about: Alleges that American firms and occupation policy are rebuilding Japanese military industry.
subfiles.summary: The article claims American capital controls Japanese firms and supports renewed armaments production.

subfiles.title: Outline of Matters for Discussion with Mr. Dodge
subfiles.about: Lists questions on Japanese economic policy, occupation costs, foreign banking, and compensation claims.
subfiles.summary: Questions address government initiative, industry, public attitudes, occupation expenses, banking, and property losses.

subfiles.title: Tokyo Airgram A-109
subfiles.about: Reports occupation economic discussions and developments in labor, trade, shipping, and financial arrangements.
subfiles.summary: The airgram discusses Dodge's influence, coal miners' wages, a possible United States economic mission, and trade administration. It also covers action against the Far Eastern Freight Conference, Japanese technicians' travel, proposed shipping to Bremen, Belgian financial negotiations, and trade balance questions.

subfiles.title: Inquiry on Japanese Fair Trade Commission action against Far Eastern Freight Conference
subfiles.about: Requests details about an indictment and postponed hearings involving the freight conference.
subfiles.summary: The Department seeks the case's grounds, current status, and reasons for postponement.

subfiles.title: Report on the Japanese Recovery Program
subfiles.about: Recommends publishing a report on Japan's recovery program if it fits the publication program.
subfiles.summary: Crosby recounts consultations with the House Foreign Affairs Committee and recommends reproduction.

subfiles.title: Tokyo Airgram A-117
subfiles.about: Reports developments in occupation economic and trade administration.
subfiles.summary: The surviving OCR is severely degraded. Legible portions describe plans for a Japanese foreign trade ministry, export control licensing, and the Foreign Exchange Control Board, alongside other occupation trade discussions.

subfiles.title: Tokyo Airgram A-122
subfiles.about: Reports economic policy discussions, including a Tokyo Shibaura deconcentration dispute.
subfiles.summary: Much of the airgram is unreadable in the OCR. Its closing discussion says Tokyo Shibaura's labor union may appeal a deconcentration order and raises questions about access to court review.

subfiles.title: Comments on Mr. Hutchinson's statements concerning deconcentration
subfiles.from: Cloyce K. Huston, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Challenges Hutchinson's account of Japan's deconcentration program and zaibatsu dissolution.
subfiles.summary: The mission disputes claims about hearings under the Deconcentration Law, the number of companies likely to be broken up, and the extent of zaibatsu liquidation. It argues that several statements overstate completed reforms and notes the Review Board's refusal to treat Hutchinson's remarks as official.

subfiles.title: Tokyo Airgram A-131
subfiles.about: Reports on a planned McEvoy speech and press discussion of Marquat's foreign business proposals.
subfiles.summary: The airgram discusses obtaining McEvoy's San Francisco speech and quotes commentary on Marquat's efforts to ease restrictions on foreign business in Japan. Later pages are largely unreadable.

subfiles.title: Airgram on Japanese economic and trade matters
subfiles.about: Discusses foreign trade matters, though the OCR obscures most details.
subfiles.summary: Legible fragments refer to trade representatives and Japanese technicians.

subfiles.title: Tokyo Airgram on industrial production and coal
subfiles.about: Reports a revised industrial production index, coal output prospects, and other economic matters.
subfiles.summary: The airgram describes an expected revision of the industrial production index and coal expert Paulick's doubts that Japan can meet its 42 million ton target. Later, poorly preserved sections address trade and Belgian monetary arrangements.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding “Public Relations Aspects of the Economic Stabilization Program in Japan”
subfiles.about: Sends an unofficial State Department research paper for Army consideration.
subfiles.summary: Barnett suggests sharing the paper's recommendations with occupation officers in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Public Relations Aspects of the Economic Stabilization Program in Japan
subfiles.about: Proposes ways to explain the stabilization program and reduce Japanese opposition to it.
subfiles.summary: The paper proposes an educational campaign explaining stabilization, United States aid, and anticipated gains in living standards. It urges attention to labor's concerns and suggests releasing surplus textiles, easing taxes for low wage earners, allowing some wage flexibility, and planning unemployment relief and public works. Its discussion continues beyond page 500.
